clues.text: This landmark began as a place of worship, later became a civic institution, and has in recent decades resumed a role tied to its original purpose.
Visible from a significant water route used by traders and pilgrims, its form was shaped by successive layers of political and religious authority.
Between the end of an ancient imperial order and the beginning of a new one, its primary religious function changed, and its silhouette was altered with new vertical elements.
Its interior was renowned for a vast illuminated space, and its design was later explicitly emulated by buildings of a different faith.
A key event in the separation of two major religious traditions took place within its walls, and its most distinctive structural feature was rebuilt after a partial collapse.
A short inscription left by a foreign visitor in the distant past was discovered high on its interior walls.

reveal.title: Reveal: Hagia Sophia
reveal.summary: Hagia Sophia, in Istanbul, Turkey, was first a Christian cathedral (360–1453), then a mosque (1453–1935), then a museum (1935–2020), and was re-designated as a mosque in 2020. It was the world's largest church for over 500 years and the largest interior space when completed in 537. Its design influenced both Byzantine churches and Ottoman mosques. A Viking inscription, 'Halvdan was here,' was found in the upper gallery.
reveal.clueExplanation: Each clue narrows the field. The final clue about a foreign visitor's inscription points to the runic graffiti left by the Varangian Guard, confirming Hagia Sophia.
